text:
Cutter Gauthier has scored in 10 straight games, 19 goals in all, and Daily Faceoff noted he is the first NHLer with four hat tricks in one month. Since Oct. 29 he has twice as many goals as the entire Seattle Kraken. His latest three came in an 8-6 loss in St. Louis on Tuesday, which is how Anaheim's season goes: 3.86 goals for a game and 3.86 against. By our numbers the run is earned, 22 points in 10 games with the chances to match, though nobody shoots at that rate forever.

He gets an Avalanche team on the second night of a back-to-back and without its two best players. Nathan MacKinnon is out about a month and Cale Makar about two weeks, per Field Level Media, and Josh Manson is out too. Wednesday's 4-1 loss in Utah got nasty, and Martin Necas took a hit Yahoo Sports called scary; he's in our projections, so check the lineup. Brock Nelson has moved up beside Necas and Artturi Lehkonen, Lehkonen is on the top power play, and Sam Malinski is up to 23:23 a night on defense. Before Utah, Colorado was handling the absences well, 70% of the chances in a 4-1 win in Montreal.

The Avalanche's structure still shows up in the numbers: 53% of the expected goals (the quality of the chances) at five on five against Anaheim's 46%, and the Ducks take 4.7 penalties a game. The goaltending on both sides is the soft spot. Scott Wedgewood starts over Mackenzie Blackwood, who has 17 of 22 starts, and is at -6.9 goals saved above expected in six games after a +23.6 season. Lukas Dostal is at .858. Beckett Sennecke, with 17 points in 10 games, is off the out list and day-to-day.

Our model has Colorado ahead, 4.04 to 3.17 in expected goals, which says a lot about what it thinks of these two defenses. Our sleepers are Avs: Nicolas Roy (17% to score) and Devon Toews, 55% for a point with his minutes up to about 24 a night.
headline: Gauthier's streak meets a thin Avalanche
